items.stem: What most clearly distinguishes an agent from a single LLM prompt?

options.text: It iterates through a loop of reasoning, taking actions with tools, and observing results
options.rationale: Correct: an agent acts in a loop with tools and observations, not one static response.
Model size does not define agency.
Agents often take longer due to multiple steps.
Tool use is central to most agents, not absent.

items.explanation: Correct: an agent acts in a loop with tools and observations, not one static response.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO practices improve the reliability of a tool-using agent? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Give tools precise schemas and clear descriptions
options.rationale: Correct: clear schemas help the model call tools correctly.

options.text: Set step or budget limits to stop runaway loops
options.rationale: Correct: limits prevent the agent from looping indefinitely or overspending.

options.text: Remove all error handling to simplify the code
options.rationale: Removing error handling makes failures worse, not better.

options.text: Hide tool errors from the agent entirely
options.rationale: The agent needs observations, including errors, to recover.

items.explanation: Correct: clear schemas help the model call tools correctly.

items.stem: An agent keeps appending the full conversation to every prompt until it exceeds the context window. What is the best fix?

options.text: Summarise or prune older state so the working context stays within limits
options.rationale: Correct: context management via summarisation/pruning keeps prompts in budget.

options.text: Switch to a single LLM call with no memory
options.rationale: That removes needed state rather than managing it.
Temperature does not affect context length.
More tool calls do not solve context overflow.

items.explanation: Correct: context management via summarisation/pruning keeps prompts in budget.
